title: Linearized focusing and quantum entropy inequalities

items.title: Linearized future horizon focusing model
items.physical_scope: An adopted first-order Einstein-Hilbert semiclassical model on a fixed smooth globally hyperbolic Lorentzian four-manifold with a stationary smooth null hypersurface, compact transverse cuts, an affinely normalized complete future generator flow, a supplied Hadamard state family and one fixed stress prescription. It asserts no null energy condition, entropy inequality, solution existence, physical accuracy, or general higher-curvature focusing result.
items.statement: Adopt the first-order Einstein-Hilbert horizon equation ∂λδθ = −8πG_N δT_kk with the fixed affine normalization and future condition δθ(∞)=0. Its signed stress moment is absolutely integrable on the compact transverse cut. Terms quadratic in expansion and shear are omitted only at first perturbative order; no null-energy or entropy inequality is adopted.

references.title: Aron C. Wall, A proof of the generalized second law for rapidly changing fields and arbitrary horizon slices, Physical Review D 85, 104049 (2012), arXiv:1105.3445v6
references.locator: Complete 44-page article; §2.2, equations (14)–(23), for the stationary-background first-order Raychaudhuri equation, affine future boundary condition, expansion/area relation and twice-integrated null-stress moment. The later modular/GSL bridge is not imported.

references.title: Harvey Reall, Part III Black Holes, University of Cambridge lecture notes (2024)
references.locator: Complete 149-page lecture notes; §§4.6 and 4.8, especially equations (4.26)–(4.40), for affine null generators, screen expansion/shear and the exact null Raychaudhuri equation. The local model adopts only its stated first-order specialization.

items.title: Linearized horizon area deficit is a weighted null moment
items.physical_scope: A first-order geometric identity for a smooth compact cut of the stationary reference null hypersurface in the adopted Einstein-Hilbert model, with an affinely normalized future generator, fixed future boundary condition and absolutely integrable stress moment. The result has no sign conclusion and makes no entropy, modular-Hamiltonian, QNEC, QFC, generalized-second-law, or empirical claim.
items.statement: For the adopted stationary-background linearized focusing model, the first-order area difference δA(∞)−δA(λ) equals 8πG_N times the transverse integral of the future-weighted null-stress moment. Dividing by 4G_N gives 2π times that moment; it is a geometric normalization, not an entropy or modular-Hamiltonian identification.

references.title: Aron C. Wall, A proof of the generalized second law for rapidly changing fields and arbitrary horizon slices, Physical Review D 85, 104049 (2012), arXiv:1105.3445v6
references.locator: Complete 44-page article; §2.2, equations (16)–(23), for the first-order null focusing law, expansion/area relation, future boundary condition and transverse integral. The proof below supplies the local argument under its stated integrability assumptions.

references.title: Harvey Reall, Part III Black Holes, University of Cambridge lecture notes (2024)
references.locator: Complete 149-page lecture notes; §§4.6 and 4.8, equations (4.26)–(4.40), for the screen deformation, area expansion and exact null Raychaudhuri equation. No area theorem or entropy identification is imported.

title: Linearized focusing and quantum entropy inequalities — Examples

items.title: QNEC and QFC have different status and hypotheses
items.physical_scope: A source-scoped status distinction between selected quantum null energy inequalities and the quantum focusing conjecture. It establishes no entropy inequality, universal theorem, experimental result, or model applicability claim.
items.statement: One proved QNEC formulation bounds the null stress by a second variation of outside von Neumann entropy for free or superrenormalizable bosonic fields on stationary null hypersurfaces under the paper's hypotheses. The QFC is a distinct conjecture about null variations of a specified generalized entropy. Higher-curvature counterexamples in d ≥ 5 and model-specific two-dimensional JT results do not supply a universal QFC theorem. This page defines no entropy shape derivative and proves neither QNEC nor QFC.

references.title: Raphael Bousso, Zachary Fisher, Jason Koeller, Stefan Leichenauer and Aron C. Wall, Proof of the Quantum Null Energy Condition, arXiv:1509.02542v2
references.locator: Complete 32-page article; abstract, §2 and §§4.5–5, for the entropy second-variation statement and proof scope: free or superrenormalizable bosonic fields on stationary null hypersurfaces, with its specified field-theory assumptions.

references.title: Raphael Bousso, Zachary Fisher, Stefan Leichenauer and Aron C. Wall, A Quantum Focussing Conjecture, arXiv:1506.02669v1
references.locator: Complete 45-page article; §3.3, equation (3.10), and §5.2, for the proposed functional monotonicity and its distinction from special QNEC proofs.

references.title: Zicao Fu, Jason Koeller and Donald Marolf, Violating the Quantum Focusing Conjecture and Quantum Covariant Entropy Bound in d ≥ 5 dimensions, arXiv:1705.03161v2
references.locator: Complete 14-page article; §2, equations (2.17)–(2.19), and §4, for weak-curvature Einstein-Hilbert-Gauss-Bonnet counterexamples to unrestricted QFC in spacetime dimension d ≥ 5 and the EFT-resolution caveat.

references.title: Victor Franken, Sami Kaya, François Rondeau, Arvin Shahbazi-Moghaddam and Patrick Tran, Tests of restricted quantum focusing and a new CFT bound, arXiv:2510.13961v3
references.locator: Complete 57-page article; abstract and §1, plus §3, especially pp. 20–22, for the class of two-dimensional JT toy models, the regime-specific QFC counterexamples, and the authors' caution against interpreting them as strong evidence against the original conjecture.
